q: A 12-month-old child can do all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Copying a circle is a skill of 3 years.

q: All of the following are abnormal findings in a 7-month-old infant EXCEPT:
e: An extensor plantar response is normal until the child walks. The Moro and grasp reflexes should be gone by 6 months, and head lag after 4 months and an obligatory asymmetrical tonic neck reflex are abnormal.

q: A 2-year-old child can do all of the following EXCEPT:
e: At 2 years a child copies a vertical line; a circle is copied at 3 years.

q: Which pair shows the CORRECT stage of normal development?
e: The mature pincer grip appears at 12 months. A child pulls to stand at 9 months, hand preference is established at 2–3 years, a cross is copied at 4 years and a square at 4½ years.

q: A child can hop and stand on one leg. His age is about:
e: Hopping on one foot is a skill of 4 years.

q: A baby says "mama" and "dada" and waves bye-bye. The most likely age is:
e: Waving bye-bye and saying "mama" and "dada" appear at about 10 months.

q: The majority of children at 18 months can do all of the following EXCEPT:
e: A circle is copied at 3 years.

q: All of the following can cause motor developmental delay EXCEPT:
e: Asthma does not delay motor development.

q: A child can draw a cross by the age of:
e: A child copies a line at 2 years, a circle at 3 years, a cross at 4 years, a square at 4½ years and a triangle at 5 years.

q: All of the following are true about bottom-shuffling EXCEPT:
o: It always follows crawling on all fours
e: Bottom shufflers often skip crawling. Bottom shuffling is a familial normal variant.

q: The correct order in which children copy shapes is:
e: Circle (3 years), then cross (4 years), then square (4½ years), then triangle (5 years).

q: A child rides a tricycle at the age of:
e: Riding a tricycle is a milestone of 3 years.

q: The social smile appears at:
e: The social smile appears at 6 weeks. No smile at 8 weeks needs assessment.

q: The percentage of children walking unsupported at 12 months is about:
e: 12–13 months is the median age for walking, so about half of children walk at 12 months. The limit age is 18 months.

q: At 8 months a baby can:
e: Infants sit without support at 7–8 months.

q: A normal 6-month-old baby can NOT:
e: Crawling starts at about 9 months.

q: Which of the following is NOT a primitive reflex?
e: The parachute reaction is a protective (postural) reaction that appears at 9 months and persists for life.

q: The reflex that appears at 9 months and persists is the:
e: The parachute reaction appears at 9 months and persists for life.

q: Absence of the Moro reflex on both sides in the neonatal period indicates:
e: Absence on both sides indicates depression of the central nervous system (hypoxic–ischaemic encephalopathy, kernicterus, sepsis). Absence on one side indicates Erb's palsy or a fractured clavicle.

q: An infant lifts his head 45° when prone, smiles when encouraged and coos, but cannot sit. The most likely age is:
e: Lifting the head and chest on the forearms, cooing and smiling readily are seen at 3 months.

q: A girl dresses with help, rides a tricycle, knows her age and speaks in short sentences, but cannot copy a square. Her age is most likely:
e: Riding a tricycle, giving her name and age, and speaking in sentences are skills of 3 years. A square is copied at 4½ years.

q: A 2½-year-old says only 3 single words. Motor and social development are normal. The first investigation is:
e: Hearing loss must be excluded first in every child with speech delay.

q: A 10-month-old reaches for toys only with the right hand and keeps the left hand fisted. The most likely explanation is:
e: Hand preference before 12 months suggests weakness of the other side (hemiplegia).

q: A boy of 20 months is not walking. He has large calves and rises from the floor using his hands on his thighs. The most useful test is:
e: Late walking with Gowers sign and enlarged calves in a boy suggests Duchenne muscular dystrophy; the creatine kinase is very high.
